species.label: Frog
species.plain: The African clawed frog, with 36,429 genes in UniProt's reference proteome, on two sets of chromosomes, L and S. This is what the family signatures of Cells' units find among the 35,004 proteins shown.

method: The frog's proteins are those of UniProt's gene-by-gene set of the reference proteome UP000186698 (release 2026_04), 36,429, which lists the two copies of a gene, on an L and on an S chromosome, as two genes. Both copies are shown, each as its own protein: nothing read here says they are one, and no pair is merged.

Where a gene has a reviewed entry and unreviewed entries in that set, only the reviewed one is shown (decided on 19 November 2026): 1,425 unreviewed entries of 1,410 genes are not shown, and the reviewed entry names them on the shelves. A gene is the entries tied together by the NCBI gene identifiers UniProt gives them. 35,004 proteins are shown, 3,523 with a reviewed entry and 31,481 with an unreviewed one.
476 genes still stand twice or more among them, with 952 unreviewed entries and no reviewed one, since no record read here picks between them.
Licences were read before anything was copied; each is stated in sources.
Each unit's family was taken from its own human candidates, by the same InterPro signatures that the other species' atlases ask. The build checks that the candidates carry them.

Each signature was looked for among the InterPro entries UniProt gives each protein. A unit counts as found only where a protein carries the signature of a family that makes the machine itself; an accessory family alone does not make it found.

A frog protein is listed because its own entry carries the family's signature, never because its gene's symbol looks like that of a human candidate. Both copies of a gene are listed where both carry it.

Each product says, apart, how it was found and what its entry is. Found: by the signature of a family that makes the machine itself, which makes it a candidate by family, or only by that of a family that goes with the machine (a regulator, or a subunit that makes no channel or pump by itself), which makes it no candidate for the machine's own work. Its entry: reviewed by a curator, or annotated automatically; that says how the entry was written, not that the protein does the unit's work.
Several units of one family (the Kv1 channels) list the same proteins, and nothing here says which protein does which unit's work.
No similarity search was run, no source of orthology was read, and nothing is called an ortholog.

U01.note: 13 proteins of its 35,004 carry the signature of voltage-gated sodium channel alpha subunits (IPR001696): LOC108701352, LOC108701353, LOC108701357, LOC108701767, LOC108702183, LOC108702974, LOC108707553, LOC108708999, LOC108718723, LOC108719816 and 3 more.
